title: City of Johnstown WWTP
warnings: ⚠️ TREATING THIS AS "NEW ALBANY'S PLANT" IS AN [inference], NOT [verified] — AND IT IS PROBABLY WRONG. The permittee, facility name, address and county below are transcribed exactly as the instrument prints them: City of Johnstown, City of Johnstown WWTP, 470 West Jersey Street, Johnstown, Ohio, Licking County. Johnstown is a separate incorporated municipality from New Albany, in the same county (Licking) but not the same place. This file is shelved at data/extracted/oepa/new-albany/ because `new-albany` is the watershed point this corpus tracks (data/sites.yaml, issue #1279) — the shelf records CUSTODY (which site's working set this document was fetched into), not an assertion that the permit belongs to New Albany. Compounding this: New Albany's own SiteProfile (data/sites.yaml, new-albany) records its receiving water as Big Walnut Creek in the Scioto basin, while this permit's own receiving water — see below — is Raccoon Creek, a different stream. [reference] to data/sites.yaml for the New Albany profile fact; nothing in that comparison is asserted about which basin Raccoon Creek itself drains to, which this document does not state and this corpus does not otherwise establish.

WHETHER THIS PLANT HAS ANY ACTUAL CONNECTION TO NEW ALBANY IS [open]. Two distinct questions are both unresolved by any captured source in this corpus: (1) whether the City of Johnstown's sanitary sewer system carries any flow that originates in New Albany (e.g., through an intermunicipal agreement or shared sewershed at the two cities' shared Licking County border), and (2) whether the New Albany data-center campus tracked elsewhere in this corpus discharges, directly or indirectly, to this plant. This document is silent on both — it names no other municipality, no data center, and no interconnection agreement anywhere in its 66 pages (checked by grepping the full text for "New Albany" and "data center", zero hits either way). Do not cite this file as evidence for or against either question; it settles neither.

THE PERMIT NAMES A SINGLE OUTFALL — 4PC00001001 — for the plant's entire term. There is no 002, no bypass outfall, and no CSO. This is a simpler outfall structure than some other permits in this corpus (e.g. Mansfield's 001/002 split); everything below attaches to the one outfall unless stated otherwise.

AN ANTIDEGRADATION FINDING IS PRINTED ON SHEET 1: "I have determined that a lowering of water quality in Raccoon Creek is necessary. In accordance with Ohio Administrative Code 3745-1-05, this decision was reached only after examining a series of technical alternatives, reviewing social and economic issues related to the degradation, and considering all public and appropriate intergovernmental comments." This sentence is signed by the Director along with the rest of the authorization page; it is not explained further anywhere else in the permit (no fact sheet is committed — see meta.not_in_this_corpus). It reads as the water-quality justification for the facility-expansion effluent limits described in permit.facility_expansion_context and permit.schedule_of_compliance below.

A CROSS-REFERENCE IN THE EFFLUENT-LIMIT TABLE FOOTNOTES DOES NOT MATCH PART II'S OWN LETTERING. Every effluent-limit table (Initial, Interim, Final — sheets 4, 7 and 10) footnotes "Toxicity Biomonitoring - See Part II, Item U." Part II's own lettered items run A through T and stop there; T is "Biomonitoring Program Requirements" (sheet 32). There is no Item U anywhere in this permit. The cross-reference is off by one letter; a reader following it literally would not find a section U. Transcribed as printed — see permit.other_requirements_of_note.lettering_defect.

"WWPT" — the sentence gating Parts IV, V and VI reads "The stormwater conditions in Parts IV, V, and VI apply to the permittee after construction of the expanded WWPT have been completed" (sheet 45). This is the document's own typo for WWTP; transcribed as printed. Substantively it matters more than the typo: the industrial-stormwater/SWPPP obligations in Parts IV-VI are NOT YET ACTIVE. They are gated on completion of the facility expansion, whose own schedule (permit.schedule_of_compliance) puts "End Construction" no earlier than 30 months after the effective date — on or about 2027-09-01, still in the future as of 2026-08-26. See permit.stormwater_parts_iv_v_vi.

fields.permit_action: NOT STATED ON THE FACE OF THE INSTRUMENT. facility_expansion_context.note: Not a separately labeled section of the permit — assembled here from three things the document DOES say on its face: (1) the Part I,A design-flow basis note doubles between the Interim and Final effluent-limit tables, "average design flow of 1.2 MGD" to "average design flow of 2.4 MGD" (see permit.effluent_limits_001); (2) Part I,C's schedule of compliance carries a "Facility Expansion" track with its own milestones (Submit First/Second Construction Annual Report, End Construction — see permit.schedule_of_compliance); and (3) the sentence gating Parts IV-VI to "after construction of the expanded WWPT have been completed" (see permit.warnings[5]). Read together they describe a plant expansion from a 1.2 MGD to a 2.4 MGD design flow, with new effluent limits phasing in as construction completes on or about 2027-09-01. The permit never states the expansion's cost, contractor, or engineering description — those would be in the uncommitted fact sheet (see meta.not_in_this_corpus).

unchanged_across_all_three_tables.note: These parameters and limits are IDENTICAL in the Initial, Interim and Final tables.
unchanged_across_all_three_tables.monitor_only_no_limit_change: Total Kjeldahl nitrogen, nitrite plus nitrate, dissolved orthophosphate, total filterable residue — all carry a monitoring frequency and NO numeric limit in any of the three tables.

design_flow_scaled_at_final.note: Concentration limits are UNCHANGED between Interim and Final; the mass LOADING doubles because the design-flow basis doubles (1.2 to 2.4 MGD). Transcribed once per parameter with both load figures shown.

ammonia_nh3.note: Concentration limits LOOSEN slightly at Final relative to Initial/Interim even though the load roughly doubles — both effects of the doubled design-flow basis. Identical between Initial and Interim.

total_phosphorus.note: NEW LIMIT AT INTERIM, TIGHTENED AT FINAL — the one parameter whose concentration limit changes at every phase. Monitor-only in the Initial table (Schedule item 1's "interim effluent limits for total phosphorus" have not yet attached); a monthly limit appears starting with the Interim table; the Final table's monthly limit is numerically TIGHTER even though the load figure is higher (because the design-flow basis doubled).

new_at_final_only.note: Monitor-only (no numeric limit) in BOTH the Initial and Interim tables; a numeric limit appears for the first time in the Final table, alongside the doubled design-flow basis.

nitrogen_inorganic_total.note: "Total inorganic nitrogen shall be calculated as the sum of the concentration results for Nitrite Plus Nitrate and Ammonia" — a calculated parameter, not independently sampled.

pimephales_never_limited.note: Acute (61427, TUa) and chronic (61428, TUc) toxicity on Pimephales promelas (fathead minnow) stay MONITOR ONLY — 1/Year 24hr Composite, August — in ALL THREE tables, Initial, Interim and Final alike. Only Ceriodaphnia dubia (water flea) gains a numeric WET limit at Final. Whatever drove the numeric WET limit onto this plant's fathead minnow test never happens in this permit term; only the water flea does.

metals_and_cyanide_monitor_only_frequenc.note: Nickel, zinc, cadmium, lead, chromium (total recoverable), copper and free cyanide (low-level) stay monitor-only — NO numeric limit is ever added, in any of the three tables — but their monitoring FREQUENCY intensifies from 1/Quarter (Quarterly months) in Initial and Interim to 1/Month (All months) in Final. Chromium, dissolved hexavalent (01220), is the one metal already monitored 1/Month/Grab/All in every table — it does not change.
metals_and_cyanide_monitor_only_frequenc.parameters: 01074 Nickel, 01094 Zinc, 01113 Cadmium, 01114 Lead, 01118 Chromium (total recoverable), 01119 Copper — all ug/l, 24hr Composite; 51173 Cyanide, Free (Low-Level), ug/l, Grab.

schedule_cross_reference_note_narrows_by.note: Each table's own footnotes cite which Part I,C schedule items apply to it, and the citation narrows as the permit term advances. Initial table (sheet 4): "New Effluent Limits Schedule of Compliance - see Part I,C, Items 1, 2, and 3." Interim table (sheet 7): "...see Part I,C, Items 1 and 2." — Item 3 (facility expansion) dropped even though its own limits do not attach until Final, and even though Item 1's citation is KEPT despite the Interim table already carrying phosphorus's interim numeric limit. Final table (sheet 10): the schedule-of-compliance footnote is DROPPED ENTIRELY — none of Items 1, 2 or 3 is cited, consistent with every phased limit already being in force by then. Transcribed as printed; the Initial-table citation of Item 3 before that item's limits are relevant to ANY of the three tables looks like an editorial carryover, but this file does not resolve it.

sso_300.note: As printed, the 1/Month figure is a REPORTING frequency, not a monitoring one — "these overflows shall be monitored on each day when they discharge." Only SSOs reaching waters of the state (directly or through a storm sewer) are reported at this station. "All sanitary sewer overflows are prohibited." (note c).
sso_300.annual_report: An annual SSO report covering ALL overflows in the collection system (including those never reaching waters of the state) is due March 31 for the prior calendar year, with locations numbered consecutively from 301, volumes in millions of gallons, and a narrative analysis of water-in-basement (WIB) patterns by sewershed.

sludge_581.note: Two tables — Interim (sheets 12-14, effective through 30 months, 1/Year Composite, December) and Final (sheets 15-17, from 31 months, 1/Quarter Composite, Quarterly - Alt.). The metal ceilings and fecal coliform limit are IDENTICAL between the two tables — only the sampling FREQUENCY changes.

status_of_these_milestones.lapsed: Three of the seven milestone dates are in the past: the Total Phosphorus final compliance (2025-09-01), and BOTH first-annual-report items due 2026-03-01 (Mercury & WET's, and Facility Expansion's).
status_of_these_milestones.not_yet_due: The remaining four — both second-annual-report items (2027-03-01) and both 30-month final items, Mercury & WET final compliance and Facility Expansion end construction (2027-09-01) — are still in the future as of 2026-08-26.
status_of_these_milestones.what_is_not_established: WHETHER ANY OF THE THREE LAPSED MILESTONES WAS FILED. Nothing in this corpus establishes that — no submittal, no acknowledgment, no violation notice, and no ECHO/ICIS extract for this facility is committed. "Past due" here means the date has passed, NOT that the City of Johnstown missed it.
status_of_these_milestones.how_to_close_it: A public-records request to Ohio EPA Central District Office for the 05699 (total phosphorus) and the two 2026-03-01 progress-report submittals under permit 4PC00001 would settle whether the interim phosphorus limit was met and how construction on the facility expansion was progressing at the one-year mark.

lettering_defect.note: See permit.warnings[4]. Part II's own items run A through T; T is Biomonitoring Program Requirements (sheet 32). Every effluent-limit-table footnote pointing readers to the biomonitoring section calls it "Item U" — a letter that does not exist in this document's Part II. All other cross-references checked (Free Cyanide -> O, Mercury -> P, Orthophosphate -> Q, sludge sections -> K/L/M/N) match Part II's actual lettering.

biomonitoring_program.text: "The permittee shall continue to implement an effluent biomonitoring program to determine the toxicity of the effluent from outfall 4PC0001001." (as printed — the item text drops a leading zero from the outfall number, printing "4PC0001001" instead of "4PC00001001"; transcribed as printed.)
biomonitoring_program.testing: Chronic and definitive acute toxicity tests for the duration of the permit, on both Ceriodaphnia dubia and Pimephales promelas, per Ohio EPA's "Reporting and Testing Guidance for Biomonitoring," July 1998 or current revision. The SOP (or verification of its submittal) was due no later than three months after the effective date — on or about 2025-06-01 [inference].
biomonitoring_program.significance: "Continue to implement" implies the biomonitoring program predates this permit action. What drove Ohio EPA to write a numeric Ceriodaphnia WET limit into the Final table (see permit.effluent_limits_001.new_at_final_only) was presumably measured under whatever instrument preceded this one — which this corpus does not hold (see meta.not_in_this_corpus.prior_revision).
